mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain deeply depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, weekday trips to shops and restaurants will stay suppressed, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above the prior four-week mean for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below -60 and RESIDENTIAL remains above +20.

mechanism_narrative: A further week-on-week drop in TRANSIT of more than 2 points indicates additional travel suppression or service curtailment, which will push RETAIL_REC down within one week as discretionary trips fall immediately.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week after a TRANSIT week-on-week drop greater than 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays less negative than RETAIL_REC by at least 30 points, households are still making only essential trips, so nonessential retail visits will remain weaker and RETAIL_REC will drift lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds RETAIL_REC by at least 30 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining at least 30 points above RETAIL_REC.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS remains near its current collapse while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, outdoor leisure substitution is not translating into broader outings, so retail-and-recreation visits will continue edging lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises for at least two straight weeks while PARKS stays below -70 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +25.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stops falling and begins a recovery from its current low base, commuting-linked shopping should follow with a lag, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 3 points from the weekly mean
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises by at least 3 points but RETAIL_REC does not improve relative to the prior four-week mean within four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lived rebound in PARKS over the next week would indicate weather-driven outdoor activity, and that same improvement would spill into nearby retail trips, raising RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by 5 points or more week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS rises by 5 points or more week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not improve within the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain highly suppressed, people anchor routines at home and defer discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC will stay lower over the next four weeks than in the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -80 and WORKPLACES remains below -65.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM becomes less negative while RETAIL_REC does not, the snapshot reflects essential-trip concentration rather than broad reopening, which will keep retail-and-recreation mobility flat to lower over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -45 while RETAIL_REC stays below -85
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -45 and RETAIL_REC improves within one week instead of staying flat or falling.
